items.title: SpaceX signs $1.1 billion-per month computing deal
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Senior Autos Reporter Pras Subramanian joins Market Domination host Ines Ferré to report that SpaceX (SPCX) has signed a $1.1 billion-per month AI computing deal. The move will bring the company closer to its $100 billion annual recurring revenue target this year, according to CFO Bret Johnson.

items.title: What a Republican 'wipeout' in the midterm elections means for investors
items.summary: Veda Partners managing partner and director of economic policy Henrietta Treyz outlines the type of policy shifts that could affect investors most if the Republicans end up "wiping out" in the midterm elections.

items.title: What Are You Really Paying For Reddit's Ad Growth?
items.summary: Reddit (RDDT) stock is down about 35% over the past twelve months. Yet at about $155 it still trades at about 26.5 times trailing adjusted earnings, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back. The forecast that makes Reddit look cheaper does not need wider margins. It needs advertising to keep growing while search referrals stay volatile.

items.title: SCHD’s 3% Yield Hides a $216,000 Decade-Long Performance Gap Investors Miss
items.summary: Most SCHD holders track the quarterly payout and call it a win, but a decade of reinvested dividends tells a story the fund's marketing materials never mention. The yield looks safe until you compare the account balance.

items.title: How Far Could Alphabet Stock Move On You In A Year?
items.summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) stock trades at about $332, and options expiring roughly a year out price a 68% probability range running from roughly $233 to roughly $474. That floor sits just under the stock's 52-week low of $235.96, while the ceiling clears its 52-week high of $402.12. Yet, a range this wide is close to normal for these shares, not a sign of unusual fear.

items.title: How Far Could Meta Stock Swing While Its Data Center Bill Climbs?
items.summary: At about $644.38 a share, Meta Platforms (META) stock carries options that price a range from roughly $418 to $993 for about a year out. The floor of that band would take about a third off a position, and the ceiling would add more than half. Wide as it is, the range carries only a normal premium over how much the shares actually moved in the past year.
